document.author: Claude (architect)
document.purpose: Reference contract for two specified-pending-execution tasks. When execution begins, this document is the binding contract: approach, scope, stop conditions, verification. The approach for each task was researched against the actual Prism schema and Lovable codebase state at creation time.
document.scope_note: Created per H's request 2026-06-08 after G3a (L0 soft merge) was prioritized as the first task. These two tasks are NOT in scope of the G3a migration; they execute independently when prioritized.

tasks.problem_statement: The پیگیری (Follow-up) tab displays ticket information with English field names and English criterion names, while the rest of the app is in Persian. Operators using the Persian UI see English labels for criterion, priority, status, type. This breaks the Persian operator experience and is the second of three completeness gaps H identified on 2026-06-08.
tasks.user_visible_symptom: Open پیگیری tab. Tickets show English labels like 'priority: high', 'criterion: parent_company_disclosure'. Operators must mentally translate to act on tickets.

research_findings.evidence: State of Affairs section 1.7: 'name_persian text -- bilingual support'; knowledge base confirms criteria table has name_persian column

research_findings.finding: public.tickets view currently does not expose criterion_name_persian
research_findings.evidence: Migration 20260608040000 (M4+M5) added public.tickets as a passthrough from private.tickets; no join with private.criteria
Current OpenTab.tsx (post-G3a) dumps every field of each ticket row, English-named columns appear as-is

research_findings.finding: The original ticket question/notes text was researched in English
research_findings.evidence: private.tickets data inserted via bridge from English-language research runs; translating the original question text is a separate batch task

design_decisions.decision: Add criterion_name_persian to public.tickets view (single source of truth at the view layer)
design_decisions.alternative_rejected: Client-side mapping table (English→Persian) — rejected because data already has name_persian; mapping at view is more honest and avoids drift

design_decisions.decision: Static UI labels (priority, status, type) are translated in OpenTab.tsx component (UI layer)
design_decisions.rationale: These are not data; they are UI chrome. Belongs in the component.

design_decisions.decision: Original ticket question text remains in English in v1
design_decisions.rationale: Translation is a separate batch task. For v1, the criterion_name_persian label provides Persian context; the English question text appears below it with a Persian framing phrase ('سؤال باز:').

design_decisions.decision: Fallback when name_persian is null: use English name with a visual marker
design_decisions.rationale: Defensive; surfaces missing translations rather than failing silently

approach.summary: Two diffs: (a) a small migration updates public.tickets view to JOIN private.criteria and add criterion_name_persian + criterion_section_persian columns; (b) OpenTab.tsx is updated to use the new Persian column as the primary card label and to translate static labels.
approach.migration_sketch: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.tickets AS SELECT t.*, c.name_persian AS criterion_name_persian, c.section AS criterion_section FROM private.question_back_tickets t LEFT JOIN private.criteria c ON c.criterion_id = t.criterion_id WHERE t.status <> 'resolved'; (exact column list to be confirmed against current view definition during execution)
approach.ui_changes: In src/components/tabs/OpenTab.tsx: (1) replace the raw Object.entries dump with structured render that puts criterion_name_persian as card title, (2) translate label strings ('priority' → 'اولویت', 'status' → 'وضعیت', 'type' → 'نوع'), (3) wrap English question text in a Persian frame: 'سؤال باز: {english_text}'.

scope_in: Add criterion_name_persian and criterion_section to public.tickets view
Update OpenTab.tsx to use Persian labels and Persian criterion name
Add fallback when name_persian is null
Keep ticket count and structure unchanged
scope_out: Translating the original English question/notes text content (separate batch task)
Adding new ticket fields beyond Persian labeling
UI redesign of the ticket card (only label/text changes)

implementation_steps.action: Inspect current definition of public.tickets via SELECT pg_get_viewdef('public.tickets'::regclass, true);
Write migration that CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.tickets with the join + new columns, preserving all existing columns
PR for migration. Acceptance test: SELECT count(*) FROM public.tickets WHERE criterion_name_persian IS NOT NULL > 0
Lovable prompt (sent via chat assistant) that updates OpenTab.tsx with structured render + Persian labels + fallback. Use file-attachment pattern not inline JSX (markdown rendering strips tags).
Verify on preview: open پیگیری tab, confirm criterion names in Persian, static labels in Persian, ticket count = previous count

stop_conditions: OpenTab displays criterion_name_persian as primary card label (not English name)
Static labels (priority, status, type) are in Persian
Original English question text appears with a Persian framing phrase, not bare English
Ticket count in پیگیری unchanged from before the change (no rows lost)
When criterion has no Persian name, fallback marker is visible (not silent failure)

verification_queries.name: criterion_persian_populated
verification_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM public.tickets WHERE criterion_name_persian IS NOT NULL;
verification_queries.expected: should be > 0; ideally equal to ticket count if all criteria have Persian names

verification_queries.name: ticket_count_unchanged
verification_queries.expected: same as before migration (38 at time of spec, or whatever the count was)

verification_queries.name: view_columns_complete
verification_queries.sql: SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='tickets' ORDER BY ordinal_position;
verification_queries.expected: all original columns plus criterion_name_persian and criterion_section

risks.risk: Some criteria may have null name_persian
risks.mitigation: Fallback in UI: show English name with visual marker (e.g., italic + question mark). Also flag as a data-cleanup task.

risks.risk: View change may break PostgREST schema cache
risks.mitigation: Migration ends with NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';

risks.risk: Tickets that have null criterion_id (rare but possible) will have null criterion_name_persian
risks.mitigation: UI fallback: show 'بدون معیار مشخص' label

tasks.estimated_effort: 1 session, ~45 min: 15 min migration write + apply, 30 min Lovable prompt + verification

tasks.title_fa: حلقه‌ی بسته‌ی پیگیری: ثبت نتیجه و اتم‌سازی
tasks.title_en: Closed-loop follow-up: submit result and atomize
depends_on: T2 recommended but not strictly required
tasks.problem_statement: The cockpit currently presents tickets as read-only items. Operators can see what is missing but cannot record what they found. Per H 2026-06-08: 'بهتر است جایی برای وارد کردن نتیجه پیگیری و ارسال ان در پشت صحنه به سوپا بیش جهت اتمایزینگ و توزیع اتم‌ها در جای مناسب وجود داشته باشد.' The cockpit must close the loop: operator researches the answer, submits the result, the result is inserted as a new atom in the knowledge graph and properly attributed.
tasks.user_visible_symptom: Ticket cards in پیگیری have no input mechanism. The operator must use another system (or do nothing) to record results, which means the knowledge graph never receives the answer.

research_findings.finding: private.atoms is append-only via M2 triggers but INSERT is allowed
research_findings.evidence: Migration 20260608030000 (M2) installs BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers; BEFORE INSERT is not blocked

research_findings.finding: M3 chain_hash is computed automatically via BEFORE INSERT trigger
research_findings.evidence: Migration 20260608020000 (M3) installs atom_compute_chain_hash as BEFORE INSERT trigger; new atoms get correct chain hash without manual computation

research_findings.finding: atoms.source_id is NOT NULL; every atom must reference a source row in private.sources
research_findings.evidence: State of Affairs section 1.4: 'source_id uuid NOT NULL'

research_findings.finding: private.question_back_tickets has a status column; updating to 'resolved' is allowed (tickets are not append-only)
research_findings.evidence: Tickets table not protected by M2 triggers (only atoms are)

research_findings.finding: Anon role currently has SELECT on public.* views but EXECUTE permission on RPCs is controlled per-function
research_findings.evidence: Migration 20260608050000 (M6) grants anon SELECT on public.* + EXECUTE on public.dossier. New RPCs require explicit GRANT EXECUTE.

design_decisions.decision: Use a single RPC function public.submit_ticket_result that wraps all four operations (find-or-insert source, insert atom, mark ticket resolved, return atom_id)
design_decisions.rationale: Atomicity. If any step fails, the whole submission rolls back. Single network call from UI. Single permission to grant.

design_decisions.decision: Find-or-insert source by URL: if a source with that URL exists, reuse; otherwise insert new
design_decisions.rationale: Avoid source table pollution. The operator-supplied URL is the natural unique key for source dedup.
Trust weight matters for downstream evidence aggregation. Operator knows context. Default 'secondary' (not 'primary') is conservative.

design_decisions.decision: Language is detected from operator input or defaults to 'fa' (Persian)
design_decisions.rationale: Persian operator most likely writes Persian. Detection by simple character check if needed.

design_decisions.decision: On successful submission, the resolved ticket disappears from the پیگیری tab (filter on status <> 'resolved')
design_decisions.rationale: Operator gets visual confirmation; queue shrinks; resolved tickets remain in DB for audit

design_decisions.decision: Anon EXECUTE permission is granted in solo phase
design_decisions.rationale: Consistent with M6 solo-phase access model. When second user is added, this is revoked along with other anon access.

approach.summary: Three diffs: (a) a migration creates public.submit_ticket_result RPC function with full body and GRANT EXECUTE to anon; (b) OpenTab.tsx ticket card gets an inline expandable form (textarea + URL field + submit button); (c) on success, the ticket is removed from the list optimistically.
approach.rpc_signature: public.submit_ticket_result(p_ticket_id uuid, p_result_text text, p_source_url text, p_source_class int DEFAULT 2, p_language text DEFAULT 'fa') RETURNS jsonb
approach.rpc_body_sketch: BEGIN: SELECT entity_id, criterion_id INTO ... FROM private.question_back_tickets WHERE ticket_id = p_ticket_id AND status <> 'resolved'; IF NOT FOUND raise; SELECT source_id INTO v_source_id FROM private.sources WHERE url = p_source_url LIMIT 1; IF NOT FOUND INSERT INTO private.sources(url, class, language) VALUES (...) RETURNING source_id INTO v_source_id; INSERT INTO private.atoms(entity_id, criterion_id, claim, source_id, source_class, language, valid_from, status) VALUES (v_entity_id, v_criterion_id, p_result_text, v_source_id, p_source_class, p_language, now(), 'active') RETURNING atom_id INTO v_atom_id; UPDATE private.question_back_tickets SET status='resolved', resolved_at=now(), resolved_atom_id=v_atom_id WHERE ticket_id=p_ticket_id; RETURN jsonb_build_object('ticket_id', p_ticket_id, 'atom_id', v_atom_id, 'source_id', v_source_id, 'status', 'resolved'); END;
approach.rpc_security: SECURITY DEFINER (runs as owner so it can write to private.*); SET search_path = private, public, pg_temp; GRANT EXECUTE TO anon (solo phase) — revoke when second user added.
approach.ui_changes: In OpenTab.tsx: ticket card gets a toggle button ('ثبت نتیجه'); expanded panel contains textarea (label 'نتیجه پیگیری'), URL input (label 'منبع'), optional source class select, submit button. On submit: call supabase.rpc('submit_ticket_result', {...}); on success: invalidate tickets query (TanStack Query); show toast 'ثبت شد'; on failure: show error and keep form open.

scope_in: Add inline form UI to ticket cards
Optimistic UI update: ticket disappears on success
Error handling: surface backend errors to operator
scope_out: Source enrichment beyond URL + class (publisher detection, etc.)
Operator approval workflow (operator IS the trusted submitter in solo phase)
Bulk submission (one ticket at a time)
Edit/undo after submission (resolved is final; operator can submit a corrective atom later but the original ticket stays resolved)

implementation_steps.action: Inspect private.sources schema: columns, constraints. Confirm find-by-url pattern works.
Inspect private.question_back_tickets schema: confirm columns status, resolved_at, resolved_atom_id exist (add via migration if missing).
Write migration that creates public.submit_ticket_result RPC with full body + GRANT EXECUTE TO anon + NOTIFY pgrst.
PR for migration. Acceptance tests T3.V1–T3.V4 (see verification_queries).
Lovable prompt: update OpenTab.tsx with form + supabase.rpc call + optimistic update + error handling. File-attachment pattern.
Verification on preview: pick one open ticket, fill form, submit, confirm: (a) toast appears, (b) ticket disappears, (c) new atom queryable in DB, (d) ticket status='resolved' in DB.

stop_conditions: RPC public.submit_ticket_result exists and is callable from supabase JS client
Operator can open form in any open ticket card
Submission with valid inputs returns success and removes the ticket from the visible list
A new atom appears in private.atoms with claim = submitted text, correct entity_id and criterion_id from the ticket
The new atom has a non-null chain_hash computed by the M3 trigger
private.verify_atom_chain_integrity() still returns clean after submission (chain not broken)
The original ticket row in private.question_back_tickets has status='resolved' and resolved_atom_id = the new atom_id
Form validates: empty result or empty URL is rejected with Persian error message

verification_queries.name: T3.V1_rpc_exists
verification_queries.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE proname='submit_ticket_result' AND pronamespace = (SELECT oid FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname='public');

verification_queries.name: T3.V3_submission_creates_atom
verification_queries.sql: After test submission, run: SELECT count(*) FROM private.atoms WHERE claim = '<test text used in submission>';

verification_queries.name: T3.V4_chain_integrity_preserved
verification_queries.expected: all rows show is_valid=true; no broken chain

verification_queries.name: T3.V5_ticket_resolved
verification_queries.sql: After test submission, run: SELECT status, resolved_atom_id FROM private.question_back_tickets WHERE ticket_id = '<test ticket id>';

risks.risk: Operator submits low-quality or wrong data; permanent atom in append-only store
risks.mitigation: Operator is single trusted user in solo phase. If wrong atom is inserted, a corrective superseding atom can be added later (no UPDATE/DELETE, but architecture supports supersede via valid_to + new atom). Document this in operator guidance.

risks.risk: find-or-insert source race condition (two concurrent submissions of same URL)
risks.mitigation: Wrap in transaction with appropriate locking. Or accept rare duplicate source rows; deduplication is a separate background task.

risks.risk: M3 chain_hash computation depends on ORDER BY recorded_at — if two atoms inserted in same millisecond they may race
risks.mitigation: Use timestamptz with microsecond precision (Postgres default); collisions are extremely rare. If race detected via integrity check failure, post-hoc fix is possible (regenerate chain hashes).

risks.risk: Anon EXECUTE permission is broad; if anon key leaks, anyone could submit fake atoms
risks.mitigation: Accept in solo phase (single user, low exposure). When 2nd user added, revoke anon EXECUTE in same PR that re-enables AuthGate. Document this in SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md transition checklist.

risks.risk: Form UX could confuse operator into submitting wrong ticket
risks.mitigation: Form is inline (attached to specific ticket card), labeled with criterion_name_persian (Persian context). Submission shows confirmation toast with ticket criterion name.

tasks.estimated_effort: 1 session, ~90 min: 30 min migration (RPC body + tests), 45 min Lovable prompt + iteration, 15 min H verification

execution_order_when_prioritized: G3a (L0 soft merge) — separate work, in progress

notes.why_t2_before_t3: T2 is smaller (one view + UI labels) and improves the operator's ability to read tickets correctly before they start answering them. Doing T3 first would mean the operator sees English labels while submitting, increasing chance of mismatches.
notes.post_t3_consideration: Once T3 is live, the data corpus will grow via operator submissions. Consider a 'recently submitted' indicator in the cockpit so operator can see their contributions. Not in T3 scope; future enhancement.
